scenes.title: History
scenes.caption: Around 200 AD, walls were built around the city that incorporated the old fort, which became a grand entrance known as Cripplegate.

scenes.title: History
scenes.caption: Records of transactions of the time show that the cemetery had been expanded several times through the acquisition of property by Jews between 1268 and 1290.

scenes.title: History
scenes.caption: The Jews were expelled from England in 1290, and on 12 July 1291 Edward I granted the site of the cemetery to Master William de Montford, who was Dean of St Paul's but seems to have held this land privately.
